negative_findings.description: No free, machine-readable bulk/open-data export of the Hungarian company register or of the annual-accounts corpus was found. The Ministry of Justice explicitly sells the beszámoló dataset ('Beszámoló állomány értékesítése'), and KSH's statisztikai számjel tool appears to support single-entity lookups only.
negative_findings.result_summary: Bulk access exists but is commercial/licensed (Céginformációs Szolgálat, Opten, D&B); no data.gov-style free dump surfaced in either hu or en searches.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Any systematic HU vendor-population screen requires a budget line or a licence negotiation; planning around 'free bulk scraping' would be both legally risky and technically unsupported.

negative_findings.description: No documented public API for e-cégjegyzék, e-beszámoló or Cégközlöny was located in this pass; commercial providers (Opten, D&B) are the likely API route but their endpoint documentation was not surfaced.
negative_findings.result_summary: Only human-facing web query forms found for the statutory portals.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Collection design must assume form-driven, rate-limited retrieval or a commercial feed, not a clean official API.

negative_findings.description: Searches did not surface Hungarian legal entities for Worldline or Nexi under those names in the aggregator layer, whereas Diebold Nixdorf Kft. and NCR Magyarország Kft. resolved immediately.
negative_findings.result_summary: Absent from search results only — this is not evidence of absence: these groups commonly operate in HU via differently named legal entities, via a branch (fióktelep), or cross-border from another EU country.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Vendor entity resolution in HU cannot rely on brand names; it needs alias/legacy-name handling (e.g. Wincor Nixdorf → Diebold Nixdorf, Bisnode → Dun & Bradstreet Hungary) and BRIS cross-border lookups.

negative_findings.description: The central beneficial-ownership register (TTNY, AFAD Act) is not publicly queryable; access is limited to authorities, supervisors and obliged service providers via AFADREG registration.
negative_findings.result_summary: Public information pages exist (NAV, MKVK, legal commentary) but the data itself is out of reach for market research.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Ultimate-owner questions must be answered from cégkivonat ownership entries, filed company documents, or licensed commercial family-tree data — not from the UBO register.

negative_findings.description: The register/filings layer covers vendors and competitors well but serves 'partnerships' and 'case studies' only indirectly.
negative_findings.result_summary: Ownership links, joint-venture entities and consortium companies are visible; commercial partnerships and bank reference cases are not, except occasionally in the kiegészítő melléklet or üzleti jelentés narrative.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: This cell should not be expected to deliver partnership/case-study evidence; those belong to procurement, press and vendor-website cells.

coverage_gaps.description: Foreign branches (fióktelep) and cross-border service providers were not systematically explored; a foreign payments vendor may serve HU banks with no Hungarian Kft. at all.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add a dedicated sweep for 'fióktelep' and 'kereskedelmi képviselet' registrations, and use BRIS 'Find a company' plus MNB/EBA cross-border notification lists to catch entity-less market presence.

coverage_gaps.description: No TEÁOR/NACE-code-driven screen of the full HU supplier population was executed — only name-based lookups of known vendors.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Define the target TEÁOR'25 code set (e.g. 6201/6202/6209/6311/4651/6612/6619), then obtain a code-filtered company list via Opten Cégtár, D&B, or a licensed Céginformációs Szolgálat extract to discover unknown challengers.

coverage_gaps.description: Other Hungarian credit/company-information houses (e.g. Crefoport, Coface Hungary, Creditreform, EMIS/CEIC-type regional databases) were not searched in this pass.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a follow-up hu+en sweep on 'cégminősítés', 'hitelinformáció', 'credit report Hungary' to complete the commercial-provider inventory and compare pricing/coverage before subscribing.

coverage_gaps.description: Historical ownership change tracking (who bought which HU vendor, when) was identified conceptually via cégtörténet and Cégközlöny archives, but no archive depth/retention limits were established.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Test how far back Cégközlöny issue archives and Opten cégtörténet reach, and record retention limits so historical M&A reconstruction is scoped realistically.

coverage_gaps.description: English-language coverage of this cell is thin by nature — the statutory portals and filings are Hungarian-only, and English guides found were mostly commercial company-formation marketing of low evidential value.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Plan for Hungarian-language parsing (mérleg/eredménykimutatás line-item vocabulary) in the collection pipeline; use the EU e-Justice HU page as the only reliable English reference layer.

brief: Hungary's company-register and filings layer is unusually strong for vendor intelligence: registration and annual-accounts publication are legally mandatory, so every vendor's HU legal entity, owners, TEÁOR/NACE activity and audited revenue sit in two free state portals — e-cégjegyzék (register, with the paid occsz certificate channel) and e-beszamolo.im.gov.hu (beszámoló search and PDF download) — with Cégközlöny carrying court-ordered formation, change and liquidation notices that flag quiet market entries and exits first. On top of this sits a mature commercial layer (Opten Cégtár and the free Nemzeti Cégtár, Dun & Bradstreet Hungary ex-Bisnode, Céginfo.hu, iCégtár) that adds ownership link-networks and parent-company resolution, plus verification layers at NAV (VAT/enforcement/debt status) and KSH (statisztikai számjel, TEÁOR), and BRIS via the EU e-Justice portal for cross-border parentage. Spot checks confirm the sector's actors resolve cleanly here — Diebold Nixdorf Kft. (ex-Wincor Nixdorf, Vecsés), NCR Magyarország Kft., and a Diebold self-service entity in végelszámolás — while Worldline/Nexi did not surface under those names, underscoring that alias, legacy-name and fióktelep handling is essential. The main constraints are that there is no free bulk export (the Ministry sells the filings dataset), no documented public API, and the UBO register is closed by law, so plan for licensed data or polite form-driven collection in Hungarian.
